answer: Peer-Anchored Jetty Topology. Each agent may attach only to peers whose local neighborhood overlaps its existing contacts by a minimum Jaccard threshold, forming a dense grove of mutually reachable neighbors before any transaction clears. An attacker must sustain that overlap on every duplicate identity, paying real bandwidth, latency, and message-relay costs per node rather than a one-time fee. Isolated clusters never reach orchard-level connectivity, so their votes and trades carry near-zero weight.
